defects.summary: In DEGRADED mode the PR body asserts a scoped question that was never asked, and labels a federated source that HAS moved as "unchanged". The `else` branch of `federated_note` (line 1650) is unconditional on `$FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE`, so when the generator predates `--only`/`--repin-source` — the exact merge-order window this branch's soft probes exist to survive — every re-pin PR for a federated consumer claims a question the run could not ask and could not answer.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED. Throwaway harness at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/adv3 — a copy of the branch with the suite's own `write_stub_generator` + `strip-scoped-flags.py` (both flags stripped, strip self-verified), run NON-dry-run against the fleet fixture. `bumporg/repo-fed-stale` is the fixture whose BOTH halves moved. Its generated PR body reads verbatim:

  **Federated sources keep their pins.** Each was put its own
  `--check-current --only <registry>` question and answered that its bundles have
  not moved, so none was named to `--repin-source`; ...
  - `bumporg/cms-platform@79d31b3` — **unchanged**

Both sentences are false: the stripped generator has no `--only` (proved by `--help`), the `if ... && $FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE` loop at line 1021 was skipped entirely, and cms-platform's bundles HAD moved. Compounding it, the run emits NO per-repo `::warning::` for this repo at all — the degraded federated report at line 1057 lives inside the `current_exit -eq 0` branch and repo-fed-stale's primary drifted, so the only signal the branch added is absent exactly where the false claim lands. Measured warnings for the whole degraded run: the two probe warnings plus one for repo-fed-current, none for repo-fed-stale.

This contradicts the branch's own ADR: docs/decisions/0009 line 93 promises "a degrade to 0005's behaviour", and 0005's wording (origin/main, script line ~1375) made no claim about a question — it said "Advancing one of these is still a human's job". The branch replaced unconditional-but-true text with unconditional-and-sometimes-false text. Fix: gate the two new `federated_note` strings on `$FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE` (and only claim a question was asked where the loop actually ran), falling back to main's wording otherwise.

defects.summary: The `--only` soft probe is a bare substring grep (line 711), not a capability check. Combined with argparse's default `allow_abbrev=True` on the real generator, a generator carrying any longer flag whose name begins `--only` silently false-positives the probe AND silently swallows `--only <registry>` as a prefix abbreviation — producing exactly the fleet-wide federated over-advance ADR 0009 exists to prevent, with zero warnings.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED, and it lands on the branch's own negative-control fixture. Harness at /tmp/.../scratchpad/adv (test `adv_false_positive`): the stub's real `--only` is removed and an unrelated `--only-bundles` added; nothing else changes. Result:

  probe: `grep -q -- '--only'` matches `--only-bundles LIST` in --help → FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE=true
  warnings emitted: NONE
  argparse: accepts `--only bumporg/cms-platform` as an unambiguous prefix of `--only-bundles` — no error, no exit 2 — and runs an UNSCOPED --check-current
  bumporg/repo-federated (stale primary + a source that is content-CURRENT but pinned behind its own HEAD): the combined verdict's `FAILED:` (the primary) is read as source drift
  log: "federated sources whose pins this re-pin advances: bumporg/cms-platform"
  proposed lock: ref=50e9f42d, sources[0].ref advanced 20bd292f → ae213059

That fixture's stated contract (test/run-tests.sh, setup_bump_repos comment) is "the primary ref advances and sources[0].ref must NOT". It moved.

Confirmed live-relevant: neither scripts/generate_skills_lock.py on agentskills' main nor on branch ag58-generator sets `allow_abbrev=False` (both use a plain ArgumentParser), so the abbreviation path is real, not stub-only. The `--repin` hard probe at line 651 has the same shape and already matches `--repin-source`. Fix: probe the capability rather than the help string — e.g. run `--check-current --only <a registry the lock does not plan>` and require the generator's own ERROR — or at minimum anchor the grep (`grep -qE -- '(^|[[:space:],])--only([[:space:]=,]|$)'`).

defects.summary: When the probe false-positives on prose alone, `head -1 <<< "$fed_out"` (line 1034) reports argparse's `usage:` banner instead of its error line, so the fleet goes red nightly with a message that cannot be diagnosed. This is the same defect commit 6744fcf fixes in the sweep, reintroduced on a newly reachable path in commit 4c505e3.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED. Harness at /tmp/.../scratchpad/adv2 (`adv_prose_false_positive`): a stub with NO `--only` flag, whose only mention of it is inside another option's help text ("check currency (a future --only will scope this)"). Result:

  warnings emitted: 0  (probe armed the gate on prose)
  every federated consumer fails: repo-fed-current, repo-fed-stale, repo-federated
  === Lock bump complete: 0 merged, 1 proposed, 6 skipped, 4 failed ===  (exit 1)
  message: "could not decide whether skills.lock's bumporg/cms-platform source is current — usage: gen-prose.py [-h] [--check-current] [--check-format] [--repin]"

argparse writes `usage: ...` on the FIRST line and `prog: error: unrecognized arguments: --only ...` on the LAST, so `head -1` drops the one line that says what went wrong. The failure is at least safe (nothing written, no lock touched, never exit 2), but a scheduled run is then permanently red with no stated cause and no `::warning::`. The branch's other commit adds a whole comment block to `sweep_bump_prs` about not discarding the reason; the same reasoning applies here. Lines 1139 and 1177 inherit the same `head -1` from main and are worth the same treatment (prefer `tail -1`, or grep for the `error:`/`ERROR:` line).

defects.summary: The scoped-question loop (line 1022) iterates `source_registries` without excluding `primary_registry`, so a lock that names its own primary registry in `sources` too becomes a permanent nightly hard failure that no re-pin can clear. On origin/main the same lock was re-pinned normally.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED. Harness at /tmp/.../scratchpad/adv (`adv_self_federating`): a fixture consumer whose skills.lock sets `sources[0].registry == registry == bumporg/agentskills`. With the flags present:

  ERROR: bumporg/repo-selffed: could not decide whether skills.lock's bumporg/agentskills source is current — ERROR: --only bumporg/agentskills: this lock names it as BOTH its primary registry and a federated source, so scoping to it has two answers
  === Lock bump complete: 0 merged, 0 proposed, 0 skipped, 1 failed ===

The generator's refusal is correct and the bumper's else-fail discipline routes it safely (nothing written), but there is no path back to green: the remedy is hand-editing the consumer's lock, and until then the run is red every night. On origin/main this lock's primary-scoped `--check-current` and combined federated check both pass and the lock is re-pinned. The branch's REVERSE direction therefore does turn a passing case into a hard failure. No such lock exists in the fleet today — the same 'no lock has that shape' caveat the script already writes at line 928 for the inverted case — which is why this is should-fix rather than blocking. One-line fix: `[[ "$reg" == "$primary_registry" ]] && continue` at the top of the loop, matching the guard the generator itself carries.

defects.summary: `test_bump_generator_without_scoped_flags` only ever strips BOTH flags, so the "BOTH, OR NEITHER" invariant the script's own comment (lines 693-698) makes load-bearing is never exercised in its one-missing form.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh line 4944 onward calls `write_strip_scoped_flags`, which cuts `--only` AND `--repin-source` together; there is no partial variant anywhere in the file. I built both partial cases myself (/tmp/.../scratchpad/adv, `adv_partial only` and `adv_partial repinsource`) and the script is CORRECT in each: exactly one probe warning fires, FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE goes false, BUMP_EXIT=1 (never 2), no argparse error reaches the log, and repo-fed-current's lock is byte-identical before and after. So this is a coverage gap, not a live defect — but the invariant is asserted only by a comment today, and a future edit that set FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE independently per flag would pass the whole suite. Cheap fix: parameterise the existing strip helper on which flag(s) to cut and call the test three ways.

defects.summary: The degraded federated report is unreachable whenever the primary ALSO drifted, because it sits inside the `current_exit -eq 0` branch (line 1054) — so the one signal the branch added for degraded mode is silent on exactly the repos where defect #1's false PR body is produced.
defects.evidence: MEASURED in the same degraded run as defect #1: with both flags stripped, the only per-repo annotation is `::warning::bumporg/repo-fed-current: a FEDERATED source has moved on ...`. repo-fed-stale — whose federated source also moved — gets no annotation at all, only `bundle has moved since 6b3a3fc — re-pin needed.` / `PR created.` The placement is inherited from origin/main (which had the same `log "WARN: ..."` inside the same branch), so this is not a regression on its own. It becomes load-bearing here because the branch escalated that line from log() to `::warning::` specifically so a scheduled run's reader would see it, and then left the half of the degraded population that most needs it uncovered.

defects.summary: A re-pin that is BOTH a digest-shape repair and a federated advance is titled, bodied and committed as shape-only, and its body's reproducibility promise is false.
defects.evidence: repin_reason=format (bump-consumer-locks.sh:1137) wins over repin_reason=federated (:1166, only reached in the else), but fed_drifted_regs is still non-empty so --repin-source fires. Built the fixture by adding `strip_digest_labels skills.lock` to the repo-fed-current seeding in a /tmp clone. Emitted title: 'chore: relabel skills.lock digests as sha256:<64 hex> (pin unchanged)'. Body (:1490): '**What changed:** the digest SHAPE stored in `skills.lock`, and nothing else ... every digest below is the same hex it was, wearing its label.' Commit message (:1406): 'the pin does not move and every digest is recomputed from the ref this lock already attests.' The actual pushed diff: sources[0].ref d57b517511ec48c6445d2e723ce6e644ecba7d4c -> fc7b83a9f848e1c8616a3a3e0c7b090a6deb3090, and cms-platform/deploy-site 2eccb319600ed838750cc4c48e8caf40b75ee8dc296c3c0412fa9d3c914ba707 -> 60d08b9d3b6e6ef3768ff14e2ad1281820928491e8da8a257824fa47ba86a83c (a different hex, not a relabel). Worst: :1503 states '**That remediation line is the command this PR ran**, `--ref` included, so you can reproduce this diff from it' while the quoted --check-format remediation carries no --repin-source, so running it does NOT reproduce the diff — the exact defect that paragraph was added to prevent. No fixture in test/run-tests.sh covers format+federated. Reachable now: the repo documents eight live bare-hex consumer locks and two live federated locks, and these PRs auto-merge on the sweep.

defects.summary: On a content+federated re-pin the PR body claims every digest came from the primary's newly pinned commit, and quotes no evidence for the source advance.
defects.evidence: Read from the real repo-fed-stale body produced by the suite: '**Every digest here is re-derived from the newly pinned commit**, materialized with `git archive` ... so the lock describes bytes that are actually published at `df57984`.' (:1572). The same PR advances bumporg/cms-platform 4090f37 -> f76aeaa and re-derives that source's digests at f76aeaa in a DIFFERENT repository; those bytes are not published at df57984. The federated branch at :1581 was deliberately worded differently for exactly this reason ('would be false of exactly the half this PR is about'), and that argument was not carried over to :1572 or :1586. Separately, fed_check_out is quoted only in the `federated` branch (:1533), so on the content+federated path the body marks a source '**advanced**' with no scoped verdict shown — an unevidenced claim in a body whose stated design is that every line is checkable.

defects.summary: An untouched comment 40 lines above the new gate asserts that nothing in this system ever advances a federated pin.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:961 still reads '--repin advances ONLY the primary `ref` — nothing in this system ever advances a federated pin.' The same script advances one at :1288-1306. The rest of that paragraph is superseded too: 'the moment a federated checkout sits ahead of its pin that FAILED: is permanent' was the stated justification for scoping the primary question, and after this change the pin is no longer permanent. The diff updated the sibling comments at :911-919 and :920-926 but left this one, so a reader going top-to-bottom meets the false absolute before reaching the loop that contradicts it. Violates the repo's own rule that a comment must not assert anything a reader cannot check.

defects.summary: source_registries is never deduped, so a lock federating one registry twice makes the bumper pass --repin-source twice and report its own bug as the lock's.
defects.evidence: mapfile -t source_registries at :897 preserves duplicates. Measured against the real ag58-generator (/tmp/nc/dup.py): a lock with two `sources` entries for org/cms under different bundle lists is written at exit 0; `--check-current --only org/cms` prints TWO `FAILED:` headlines and exits 1, so :1030 appends org/cms twice; :1289-1290 then builds `--repin-source org/cms@ --repin-source org/cms@` and the generator answers 'ERROR: --repin-source names org/cms twice; one pin per source' -> :1309 fail + FAIL_COUNT++. Fail-closed (nothing written), but the reason the scheduled run logs is the bumper's own duplicated flag, and it suppresses the generator's accurate single-spec diagnosis ('--repin-source org/cms: this lock federates that registry twice, under [one; two], each with its own pin'). It would recur every night on such a repo.

defects.summary: The new per-source PR-body slice inherits no headline/remediation guarantee from the 20-line cap, and can print a FAILED headline with its command cut off.
defects.evidence: why_note at :1533 runs `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' <<< "$fed_check_out" | head -20`. A non-primary block is 1 headline + 1 remediation + N difference lines. Simulated the exact pipeline (/tmp/fedcat.txt): with N=17 on the first drifted source, the second source's `FAILED: org/src-b's bundles have moved on ...` is the last line kept at line 20 and its `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref ... --repin-source 'org/src-b@'` is line 21 and is cut. The generator's own comment beside this contract names this arithmetic and explicitly declines to extend the guarantee: 'A scoped per-source slice would be a NEW consumer and would need its own guarantee; it does not inherit one here.' The bumper is now that consumer, with no guarantee and no test. Requires >=2 federated sources, so not reachable on today's locks.

defects.summary: The stub generator omits one refusal the real generator has: a --repin-source naming a registry the lock federates twice.
defects.evidence: The stub's apply_repin_sources (test/run-tests.sh around :792-815) refuses a duplicate spec, the primary registry, and a registry the lock does not federate — but has no branch for a registry appearing twice in `sources`, which the real generator refuses with a distinct message (measured: 'ERROR: --repin-source org/cms: this lock federates that registry twice, under [one; two] ...'). No current assertion depends on it, so nothing is falsely green today; it becomes a stub-fidelity gap the moment the duplicate-registry case above gets a regression test.

defects.summary: The stub generator lacks the real generator's `repin_source_blocker`, so the bumper's gate will build a `--repin-source` command the real generator explicitly declines to print and then refuses — and no assertion in the suite can catch it.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED against a real two-registry fixture, running /home/user/agentskills@ag58-generator's scripts/generate_skills_lock.py and the stub extracted from test/run-tests.sh side by side.

On a lock that federates one registry twice (representable, and `--check`-green per the generator's own comment at generate_skills_lock.py:796-840):

REAL, `--check-current --only org/src`: exit 1, `FAILED: org/src's bundles have moved on since ac07612e... — ... No --repin-source command is printed for it because this generator would refuse one: this lock federates that registry twice, under [cms; cms2] ...` — headline at column 0, and deliberately NO remediation command.
REAL, the bumper's very next move, `--repin --ref <old> --repin-source 'org/src@'`: exit 1, `ERROR: --repin-source org/src: this lock federates that registry twice ...`

STUB, same two commands: prints `  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --repin-source 'org/src@'` under the FAILED headline, then exits 0 having advanced BOTH entries from the one spec (measured sources refs `['618fab62', '618fab62']`).

The bumper's gate (scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1029, `grep -q '^FAILED:'`) reads only whether a FAILED line exists, never whether that block carried a repair. So it appends the registry to `fed_drifted_regs` and passes `--repin-source "$reg@"` at :1289. Against the real generator that lands on `fail "$repo_name: --repin failed"` + `((FAIL_COUNT++))` at :1310 — a red nightly and NO pull request for that consumer at all, including for a legitimately stale primary that could have been re-pinned, repeating every night until a human edits the lock.

The two halves of this two-PR change therefore disagree: agentskills says "no command is printed because I would refuse one"; _agent-guidance builds the command anyway. The scoped-question design made drift ATTRIBUTION a property of the question asked, but it did not make ACTIONABILITY one, and nothing distinguishes the two kinds of FAILED block. docs/decisions/0009's "Two newly reachable red nights" list names only the basename collision and the shrink guard; this third one is missing. This is the strongest candidate for blocking — the ADR's own *Left open* admits five consumer locks could not be read, so nobody has confirmed the fleet has no twice-federated lock.

defects.summary: The stub's `--repin-source` has no source-checkout identity probe, so every assertion about it is green against a stand-in that writes an impostor repository's HEAD under the named registry at exit 0.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED. Real generator, `--repin --repin-source 'org/src@' --source-repo 'org/src=<the PRIMARY registry's clone>'`:

  exit 1, `ERROR: .../fx/reg does not contain ac07612e..., the commit this lock pins for 'org/src' — so this checkout is not that registry, and re-pinning from it would write a commit the registry does not have (the hook then cannot fetch it, and every consumer session reports DEGRADED).`

Stub, identical argv: exit 0, `Wrote ...: 1 skills`, and the lock's `sources[0].ref` is now `915bdb04` — the WRONG repository's HEAD, written under `org/src`'s name.

The real generator's comment (generate_skills_lock.py:845-857, 941-973) records this as a measured live defect the probe exists to close. The stub reproduces the pre-fix behaviour. The bumper builds `--source-repo "$reg=${CHECKOUT_DIR[$reg]}"` from `BUMP_CHECKOUTS` (bump-consumer-locks.sh:946-948) and there is no test that a mis-keyed entry is caught — in the stub lane there cannot be one. The stub also omits the branch-name-pin refusal (`_COMMIT_SHA_RE` check) from the same predicate.

defects.summary: A `format` re-pin that also advances a federated pin produces a PR whose title and body flatly contradict its own diff — the exact defect the diff branched three other notes to prevent. No fixture covers the combination.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED by adding `strip_digest_labels skills.lock` to the repo-fed-current fixture in a throwaway clone and dumping the generated body. `repin_reason` becomes `format` while `fed_drifted_regs` is non-empty, and the body says:

  "**What changed:** the digest SHAPE stored in `skills.lock`, and nothing else."
  "...every digest below is the same hex it was, wearing its label."
  "The bundle content at the pinned ref is UNCHANGED — nothing has diverged, and this is not a currency bump."
  "**Every digest here is re-derived from the commit this lock already pinned**"

while the same body's federated_note says `- bumporg/cms-platform@e5dafd9 → bumporg/cms-platform@d33fd74 — **advanced**`, and the advanced source's digest measurably changed: `2eccb319600ed838750cc4c48e8caf40b75ee8dc296c3c0412fa9d3c914ba707` → `sha256:60d08b9d3b6e6ef3768ff14e2ad1281820928491e8da8a257824fa47ba86a83c`. The pr_title branch at :1674 also fires first, so the PR is listed as `chore: relabel skills.lock digests as sha256:<64 hex> (pin unchanged)` — while `sources[0].ref` moved.

Root cause: moved_note / why_note / derived_note / commit_subject / pr_title all branch on `$repin_reason` alone (:1471-1560, :1408-1420, :1674-1680), but `fed_drifted_regs` is an ORTHOGONAL axis. The diff's own comment at :1566-1571 states the rule it then breaks: "an unconditional sentence in a two-reason body is a contradiction waiting for the second reason to fire."

defects.summary: Same class, and reachable in the suite's OWN fixture: `repo-fed-stale`'s PR body claims every digest is published at the primary's new ref while an advanced source's digests come from a different repository. That body is never asserted.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED on the CLEAN branch tip with the suite green (533/0), by dumping `$BUMP_PR_BODY_DIR/bumporg_repo-fed-stale.body`:

  "**What moved:** `bumporg/agentskills` — `b13ec26` → `90d7d1c`."   (silent about the source)
  "**Every digest here is re-derived from the newly pinned commit**, materialized with `git archive` ... so the lock describes bytes that are actually published at `90d7d1c`."
  "- `bumporg/cms-platform@db8260a` → `bumporg/cms-platform@0d4e996` — **advanced**"

`90d7d1c` is the primary's ref; the `cms-platform/*` digests in that same diff are published at `0d4e996` in a different repository. The `federated` branch of derived_note (:1546-1550) has exactly the right wording ("re-derived from the commit its own source pins ... the halves that moved are listed below") and is simply not reached for `content`+federated. The change's own comment at :1272-1276 explains why the tail was split per branch — "the tail names the ref the digests were read at, and that is a different claim on each branch" — and then leaves the `content` tail unconditional.

The suite asserts repo-fed-stale's LOCK refs only (`both moved: one re-pin advances the primary AND the federated pin`); no assertion reads its PR body, which is why this ships green.

defects.summary: ADR 0009's cited measurement does not reproduce against the generator it ships with: two of its three bullets are checkably false, and its present-tense claim about `check_current` describes a shape the paired generator PR removed.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED against /home/user/agentskills@ag58-generator (12c2095), the generator half this ADR pairs with.

ADR bullet S2 — "only a source edited — the same headline, still naming the primary's clean sha, with the only true fact in a detail line below it". Actual: `FAILED: org/src's bundles have moved on since ac07612e..., which <lock> still pins for it ...` followed by `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref <primary sha> --repin-source 'org/src@'`. Correctly attributed to the source, naming the source's own pin. FALSE as written.

ADR bullet S3 — "all three drifted — still exactly one headline." Actual on a primary + one source both drifted: `grep -c '^FAILED:'` = 2. One headline PER drifted source. FALSE as written.

ADR Context, present tense — "`check_current` returns one flat list of differences across every source and `main` prints ONE headline anchored on the lock's top-level `ref`." The paired generator groups by source and marks the primary via `is_primary` (generate_skills_lock.py:1462-1550, 2123-2170). FALSE of the generator this ADR ships beside.

Only S1 still reproduces (measured: a primary-only drift on a federated lock still gives exit 1 and `^FAILED:`), and S1 alone is what actually justifies the decision — a `grep -q '^FAILED:'` gate still misreads it. So the decision is right and its stated evidence is stale. The generator's own comments were careful to date their reading of the bumper ("measured in _agent-guidance's scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh at 4c505e3, 2026-08-22"); the ADR did not reciprocate. Per the house rule that a comment must not assert what a reader cannot check, this is worse: checkable and wrong.

defects.summary: The stub guards `--only` on truthiness where the real generator deliberately uses `is not None`, so `--only ''` is silently ignored instead of refused — re-implementing in the stand-in the exact bug the real generator's comment records as measured and fixed, and making the stub docstring's stated refusal false.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED, identical argv to both:

  `--only '' --repin --repo <reg> --source-repo ...`
    REAL: exit 2, argparse usage (parser.error at generate_skills_lock.py:1823).
    STUB: exit 0, `Wrote ...: 2 skills` — the flag silently ignored.

The real generator's comment at :1806-1817 says exactly why: "`is not None`, never truthiness, in all three ... Testing truth let `--only ''` slip both guards and degrade a run into a DIFFERENT command silently." The stub's guards are `if args.only and not args.check_current:` and `if args.only and args.check_format:` (test/run-tests.sh, in write_stub_generator's main).

The stub's own docstring asserts the refusal that does not happen: "--only ... Refuses a registry the lock does not plan, one that is both primary and source, and any use outside --check-current." ADR 0009 repeats the overstatement: "The stub in `test/run-tests.sh` grew both flags, their refusals and the per-source `FAILED:` block."

No current bumper path passes an empty `--only`, so no assertion is weakened today — this is a parity/claim defect, not an exploitable one. The other seven documented refusals ARE at parity: I verified `--only <unplanned>`, `--only <primary+source>`, `--only` without `--check-current`, `--repin-source` without `--repin`, `--repin-source <primary>`, `--repin-source <unfederated>`, `--repin-source` twice, and a spec with no `@` all produce identical exit codes on both.

defects.summary: The new scoped-gate ERROR branch — `fail "...could not decide whether <lock>'s <reg> source is current"` plus `fed_gate_failed`/`break` — has no fixture, and it is the branch that stands between an unanswerable scoped question and acting on one anyway.
